analyst_view.overall: Early view: Benfica are 2nd under Marco Silva and score freely (30 in 11), but they keep conceding, needing a 94th-minute Pavlidis winner to beat Estrela 3-2, and goalkeeper Samuel Soares is under scrutiny. Aursnes (thigh) and Tomás Araújo were withdrawn from international duty with injuries, and Benfica host Viktoria Plzen in the Europa League on Thursday 26 November. Famalicão are 10th with interim coach Ricardo Silva after Hugo Oliveira's exit and have been knocked out of the Taça, so they arrive fresher.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean higher: Benfica's attack is the league's most productive, but Record notes their habit of conceding again in the 3-2 at Estrela. Famalicão scored four at Rio Ave recently and beat Arouca late, so they can take chances when they come.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, 6.8 for Benfica. Benfica won ten corners against just one at Estrela with 62% possession, and Famalicão are likely to defend deep at the Luz. I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Famalicão have had several red cards lately (Rodrigo Pinheiro at Braga, Gil Dias and Pedro Bondo in the cup at Paredes), but against a dominant Benfica they will mostly defend without the ball. Those balance out, so I keep to the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.0 shots. I lean a little lower: Benfica took 15 shots in their last league game, and with a Europa League game three days earlier Silva may manage the tempo. Famalicão will not have many attempts of their own at the Luz.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. At Estrela Benfica had just 5 on target from 15 attempts, and Aursnes's injury takes away some of their midfield control. I lean slightly lower.
